purpose: Fixed report fields for independent simulated participant 2; observations are from this session only.
persona: Independent simulated beginner, first introduction to RILL, interested in a small electronic dance groove.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: The empty-lane hint, labeled tools, on-screen naming keyboard and obvious Mixer controls let me finish with mouse input. Precise end trimming needed a correction and a send required several dialogs.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: The dark interface, teal waveforms and notes, readable faders and visible routing lines look cohesive. Several default track/pattern names became truncated in the fitted arrangement.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Drawing, duplicating and Mixer changes responded promptly. Native file dialogs appeared after a short delay, WAV export remained in progress for multiple screenshots, and one playback failure interrupted the session. This is a subjective lab-session rating, not a hardware benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Most controls had plain labels and useful feedback. The fine trim at a zoomed-out scale was easy to overshoot, and Add send opened a routing dialog with another + Send choice before the bus target.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: The requested audio, VST MIDI, Mixer volume/pan, mute/solo, bus/send, naming, save and both exports were all accessible. This task does not establish broader plugin compatibility or production completeness.

findings.observation: Following the Double-click for MIDI hint opened the Device library; Assign instrument created a track using Rill Lab Sine and a one-bar pattern.
Pencil drags created eight short labeled notes, and successive Duplicate clicks extended the MIDI pattern and drum clip. Fit made the expanding arrangement visible.
The first audio end trim produced a visible duration of 0:30.134. A second four-pixel drag corrected the project display to 0:30.000; exact trimming was fiddly at this zoom.
Dragging Mixer faders and pan knobs changed the displayed values to drums -8.0 dB/L15 and instrument -8.9 dB/R19. Mute and Solo showed distinct active highlights.
During Mixer work playback stopped and the banner stated Audio output stream failed or disconnected.
Clicking Retry playback restored the Pause state, an advanced transport position and lit master/instrument meters while the instrument was soloed. No audio was auditioned.
Add bus immediately created New bus. Instrument Add send > + Send > New bus produced a 0.25x Post send; the Mixer then showed Send · New bus and Bus 1 in.
Adding the send required entering the routing dialog and opening another + Send menu before selecting the already-created bus. The outcome was clear once the send appeared.
File > Rename project exposed a Keyboard button; clicking its on-screen keys and Apply name successfully set Sine Circuit without keyboard events.
Save and both export pickers prefilled Sine Circuit with the appropriate extension in session-2. Save removed the modification dot; both exports subsequently showed Exported notices.
The WAV options displayed Arrangement · 0:30 and an Include effect tails checkbox. Turning tails off visibly removed + tails before export.

outcome.status: Completed through the visible UI: named and saved a 30.000-second audio-plus-MIDI arrangement, exercised all requested Mixer controls, and saw WAV and MIDI export success notices. File contents await independent verification.
outcome.composition: At 112 BPM, repeated the supplied Circuit rhythm drum audio across fourteen bars, trimming the final copy to the endpoint. Drew a one-bar eight-note C4/C4/E4/G4/C4/E4/G4/F4 pattern and duplicated it to fourteen bars. One audio track, one MIDI instrument track, and one bus are visible.
outcome.instrument: Rill Lab Sine (Device library displayed VST3)
outcome.playback_observed: Transport advanced and track/master meters lit after Play. One Audio output stream failed or disconnected banner appeared during Mixer work; Retry playback restored advancing transport and visible meters. Playback was stopped before save/export and left stopped. No claim of heard audio.

limitations: No file contents were inspected and no audio was auditioned; independent coordinator verification follows.
Volume and pan balancing was based on visible values/meters, not a listening judgment.
Software graphics and a timer-paced virtual audio sink were used; the observed failure and speed rating do not establish physical-device behavior.
Only the installed laboratory Rill Lab Sine VST3 instrument was exercised.
Elapsed session time includes screenshot, tool and reporting overhead and is not a benchmark.

mixer_outcome.volume: Dragged both vertical faders. Circuit drums changed from -6.0 dB to -8.0 dB; New instrument changed from -2.5 dB to -8.9 dB. Values remained visible in final arrangement.
mixer_outcome.pan: Dragged the drum knob left and instrument knob right. Labels changed from C to L15 and R19 respectively.
mixer_outcome.mute: Clicked the drum Mute button; it highlighted amber in screenshot 12. Clicked it again to clear it before later work. Audible effect was not tested.
mixer_outcome.solo: Clicked instrument Solo; it highlighted in screenshot 13, with instrument/master meter activity after Retry playback. Clicked it again to clear it before save/export. Audible effect was not tested.
mixer_outcome.bus: Clicked Add bus. New bus appeared in the Mixer Buses group at 0.0 dB and centered pan, and later in the arrangement.
mixer_outcome.send: Clicked the instrument Add send, then + Send and New bus. The routing dialog showed New bus, level 0.25x and Post selected. The Mixer showed Send · New bus and the bus showed Bus 1 in. No effects were inserted and no audible bus processing was assessed.
